title: fix(init): the grove settings symlink holds a host-absolute path in a tracked file
description:
## the defect

`rhachet init` writes `.agent/.actors/actor.via.repo=ambient/brain/.claude/settings.of.grove.json` as a
symlink to the host's absolute `$HOME/.claude/settings.json` (`setRepoActorBrainDir`,
`setBrainDirSettingsLayout`). the path is tracked by git. so every install on a host whose `$HOME`
differs from the one that committed it repoints the symlink, and the tree reads dirty:

```
-/home/camper/.claude/settings.json
+/home/vlad/.claude/settings.json
```

`settings.of.repo.json` drifts the same way on its `claudeMdExcludes` entry
(`/home/<user>/.claude/CLAUDE.md`).

## the cost, measured

ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhrain#728, 2026-11-06. `rhx git.branch.rebase begin` refuses on unstaged
changes, and a lockfile refresh mid-rebase re-runs the install, so the rebase blocked twice on this
one file. a clone holds no paved way to put a symlink back (symlink and cpsafe refuse a target
outside the repo; git write commands are not paved), so each block needed a human reset. that reset
also reset the index, and silently dropped a staged change of the rebased commit to
`settings.of.repo.json`; only an integration test caught it.

## the shape of the fix

a host-absolute path never lands in a tracked file. either:
- the grove symlink is gitignored (it is host state by nature), or
- it is written relative, or resolved at read time from `$HOME`, so its bytes match on every host

and the same for the `claudeMdExcludes` home entry. the clamp: init on two hosts with different
`$HOME` leaves `git status` clean on both.

## related, other owners

- ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-ehmpathy `git.branch.rebase`: no way to set host-local files aside, so one
  drifted symlink halts the whole rebase
- ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhuild `git.crew.reset --what settings`: a reset mid-rebase also drops
  staged changes to those files; it should refuse, or preserve the index, while a rebase is open
